chat._why: The floating chat widget (P13-T5), with its answer service wired up at P15-T1 (server/chat.js). The service exists and is tested, but `apiBase` below is EMPTY, so the live site still opens the panel in its 'unavailable' state and routes the visitor to WhatsApp - the composer is never enabled. That is because the API has no host until Phase 11, not because anything is missing. Wording is owner-approved (24 Oct 2026 for the first 10 strings, 31 Oct 2026 for `ready` and `placeholderReady`). zh and en are approved text; de/es/fr/ja/ru are translations of that text and need a native read before cutover (a Phase 18 gate, now 12 strings per language), falling back to zh if any is removed.
chat._apiBaseWhy: Where the answer service lives (server/chat.js, POST /api/chat). EMPTY means there is no service: the composer stays disabled and the panel opens in its honest 'unavailable' state, which is exactly what P13-T5 shipped and what the live site keeps doing until the API is hosted at Phase 11. Set it to the API origin with NO trailing slash and no path - 'http://localhost:4000' to try it locally, the hosted origin after Phase 11. Because the renderer reads this at build time, turning the chat on is a data edit plus a re-render, never a code change.

grounding._why: Everything the chat answer service (server/chat.js) is allowed to tell a visitor. FACTUAL ONLY, by owner decision 31 Oct 2026: product identity, price, availability, category, where its page is, testing and certification, shipping, how to reach a person. NOTHING about efficacy, dosage, symptoms, treating a condition or taking a product with medication - those hit the approved refusal string above. A product's `desc` is efficacy copy on every one of the six products, so it is blocked in CODE (server/chat.js FORBIDDEN_FIELDS) and cannot be re-enabled from here.
grounding._faqWhy: faqIds is an ALLOWLIST and the default is deny: an FAQ added in the admin does not reach the bot until its id is added here, on purpose. Only 3 (heavy-metal and pesticide testing) and 4 (Hong Kong shipping times) are factual. 1 says PSP is 'proven' to aid immune function; 2 is a dosing protocol including a treatment-course dose; 5 answers 'can I take this with Western medicine or conventional treatment' with 'yes, it reduces side effects'; 6 makes an absorption claim. Those four are health claims that BUILD_TASKS P13G-T2 says cannot be presumed to be the client's own words, and they stay out until that review happens. The `cat` field does NOT separate factual from clinical - 3 and 5 are both 'Safety & Testing' - which is why this is a list of ids and not a list of categories.

chromeText._why: The site chrome - top bar, nav, announcement, footer - is NOT modelled as sections: renderer/chrome.js lifts it verbatim out of a live page (assets.chromeFrom), which is a stopgap recorded in renderer/render.js. That means its wording is not a tree field and cannot be translated the way page content is. This map is how a non-primary language gets a translated chrome: renderer/chrome.js substitutes these strings in text nodes and in alt/title/aria-label/placeholder attributes. When the chrome finally becomes sections or a shared partial, this map is what it has to carry. Language NAMES in the switcher (中文, 日本語) are deliberately absent - each language is shown in its own script, which is what the live page does and what users expect.
